title: Sector shapes landed: sectors 1-3 are pulses with a breath, THE PRESS and every sector after it a filled lane (an alive target, a total and a burst, streamed), every count in bodies off the row, hard cores by share; the soft factor, the stampede's multipliers and the Pearl build-up's count thinning retired (owner, 2026-10-15: 'both by sector', the switch at sector 4, 'approved, build it')
context: Owner, 2026-10-15, the rework after one branch (2026-10-15-one-branch-and-the-rework-ahead): '1) the difficult progression, 2) the timing of waves (since they are smaller), 3) confirm that we can have up to 1200 enemies as in our dev lab tests, 4) progression and story line'. Asked the first design question (what a late sector should feel like under the Pearl set) he chose (c) both by sector; asked where the flow starts, sector 4 THE PRESS (its brief already said 'The lane is never empty now.'); asked for approach 1 (shape tables with absolute sizing) over capping today's multiplying ladder or a rate-based spawner; 'Approved, build it'. Spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-sector-shapes-design.md, plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-15-sector-shapes.md. THE BASELINE, on paper (scratch paper-baseline.mjs through the game's own modules): a wave's count was the ladder's plan times the threat, times the soft factor (SECTOR_TIMING.soft: x2 at sector 1, +1 a sector, x8 from sector 7), times the invasion surge inside the ladder (wave 9 and past), times the stampede (a trickle capped at 24, a flood x3), then the Pearl build-up kept 15% to 100% of the single bodies with every squad kept whole. Per breach per wave after the build-up: S1 2/10/26/158 (392 a sector), S2 5/10/67/326 (816), S3 16/10/115/542 and the swarm 360, S4 37/10/102/422 (1,142), S5 side 266/78/130/744 and gate 266/10/130/2,162 (3,786), S7 9/8/133/761/1,103/24 a side (4,447), S8 36/7/889/3,640/1,556/20/1,645/4,996 a side (25,578), S9-S10 up to 5,452 a wave and 30,000 to 32,000 a sector. Three findings: the sizes were multiplied, not designed, and from sector 8 the crowd cap (1,500 at best, a 400 floor under a pile) and the Pearl pool dripped a 30,000-body sector out as a long undifferentiated stream whose length nobody chose ('the waves are smaller'); the build-up skipped squads, so sector 5 opened with 266 bodies on a wave meant to be at 15%; the trickle's 24-body cap against 12-second pulses left sector 8 alternating floods of thousands with drips of 7. Measured headless (--sector-probe PLAY=1, an ideal defender culling every 2 s): pulses every 15 s whatever the field; a queue of 816 released at once put 1,014 alive at sector 5's last wave, 858 put 1,573 at sector 6's; at sector 8 the cap and the pool held the floods to 400-617 alive with hundreds queued.
outcome: src/domain/sector-shape.js (pure): sizeWave (a ladder plan at an exact count, coreShare of it cored from the plan's cored types in their proportions, one of each while it fits, none at share 0, the rest soft, largest-remainder rounding, the plan's order), pulseBodies, flowWaves, pulseDue (a sector's first pulse at once; then `pulse` seconds after the last release AND the field at or under breath.at of that pulse's size, or breath.max after it whatever is alive), flowDue (the lane under its target), flowTarget (under the crowd cap), streamOffsets. src/content/sectors.js: every row says its shape in bodies. S1 THE LANE pulse [10, 20, 30, 50] a breach, pulse 12 s, breath 25%, max 60 s; S2 THE LONG LANE [20, 35, 50, 90], 10 s, max 55; S3 THE CANYON [30, 50, 70, 120] on its one gate breach (the swarm unchanged), 10 s, max 50, coreShare 0.03; S4 THE PRESS flow alive 450 / total 1,800 / burst 150 / pulse 6 s, coreShare 0.03; S5 THE SIDE WALL 550 / 2,400 / 180 / 6, 0.05; the held sectors (SECTOR_HOLD, THE CANYON AGAIN over it) 650 / 3,000 / 200 / 6 stepping +40 alive and +300 total a held sector, 0.05; THE BACK DOOR 700 / 3,600 / 220 / 6 (the feast first), 0.05; BOTH WALLS 850 / 4,800 / 250 / 5 with its 2 barbed on every burst, 0.08; the generated sectors +75 alive a sector to aliveCap 1,200 (the column the frame holds, 2026-10-15-pearl-crowd-measured-headed) and +600 total. A flow's waves planned per breach are ceil(total / breaches / burst) (src/domain/sectors.js sectorDef, `shaped`), so HELD, QUICK HANDS, the forfeit and the Pearl pace climb keep working. src/fx/sector-run.js: waveOf sizes the ladder's plan off the row (the ladder keeps choosing the types: the new-contact cadence), the stampede marks wave 2 a trickle and wave 4 a flood in a pulse sector without multiplying (src/domain/stampede.js), a flow's burst is streamed over its pulse (queueOf, streamOffsets) and packed into squads when the sector's target is a squads' wave; canRelease asks the shape (the breath, or the lane under its target, clamped by crowdTrace.cap from src/fx/crowd-gate.js) with the stall rule on top; pulseGap is 0 for a flow (the stream is its own gap, the controller arms the next pulse as the last stream leaves the queue). Retired: SECTOR_TIMING.soft/softStep/softBase (aliveBudget stays as the campaign board's guard), SECTOR_STAMPEDE.size/trickle/trickleMax/tierSize/tierCores and the fallback, PEARL_WAVES.scale (src/fx/creature-enemies.js `climb` paces only; state().waves carries the last wave's climb). The new tables on paper: S1 opens with 20 on the field and peaks at 100, S2 180, S3 120 and the swarm, S4-S10 flow targets 450, 550, 650, 700, 850, 925, 1,000. No change in src/td-tab.js (6,124 of 6,400). Headless readings of the new shape (--sector-probe PLAY=1): see the evidence. Waiting on the owner: every number by eye on :8159 (the pulse lists, the breath's share and ceiling, the flow's targets, totals and bursts, the core shares), and whether THE PRESS's switch reads as the story's escalation.
alternatives: Cap today's multiplying pipeline per sector (a wave maximum and an alive maximum over the ladder, the soft factor and the stampede): rejected; a 5,000 plan capped to 600 is still unreadable and a sector of 30,000 is still a drip whose length nobody chose.

A rate-based spawner for everything (bodies a second, pulses by modulating the rate): rejected; the cleanest flow, but the breach books (HELD, QUICK HANDS, the forfeit, the build-up) go with the waves, and it is the largest rewrite.
The switch at sector 5 (THE SIDE WALL) or at THE BACK DOOR: the owner chose THE PRESS; its brief already said the lane is never empty.
Keep PEARL_WAVES.scale and fix the squads: rejected; with the row sizing every wave in bodies a second count dial is a second truth.
evidence: node test/sector-shape.mjs, node test/sectors.mjs, node test/sector-run.mjs, node test/stampede.mjs, node test/pearl-enemies.mjs, node test/pearl-motion.mjs, node test/back-omens.mjs; npm test (257), npm run check (the architecture guard, td-tab 6,124 under 6,400), npm run build

--sector-probe PLAY=1 (an ideal defender culling every 2 s, headless) on the new tables, 2026-10-15: S2 pulses at 8, 24, 78 and 96 s (40 bodies, then the trickle of 70 dripping one every 1.3 s from 24 to 68 s, then 94, then the flood 114 with its cores), the third only after the trickle had drained and the pulse passed; S5 bursts every 12-14 s (two mouths, 360 bodies packed into ~170 entries each pulse), the field at a steady ~100 entities over the leftovers, seven bursts a breach and SECURE at 94 s; S8 the back mouth first, the gate at 26 s, bursts every 13 s with their barbed, nine a breach, SECURE at 151 s; S9 bursts of 250 a mouth. Before (the baseline on 690b03b5): pulses every 15 s whatever the field, 1,014 alive at S5's last wave and 1,573 at S6's, the trickles 7-24 bodies
